sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛtvā vivāhaṃ tu kurupravīrās; tadābhimanyor muditasvapakṣāḥ viśramya catvāry uṣasaḥ pratītāḥ; sabhāṃ virāṭasya tato 'bhijagmuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having performed the marriage, the Kuru heroes — their own side gladdened on account of Abhimanyu — rested for four dawns and then, refreshed, proceeded to the hall of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: sabhā tu sā matsyapateḥ samṛddhā; maṇipravekottamaratnacitrā nyastāsanā mālyavatī sugandhā; tām abhyayus te nararājavaryāḥ
english: That hall of the lord of the Matsyas was splendid — adorned with the finest gems and precious stones, furnished with seats, garlanded, and fragrant. Into it entered those foremost of noble kings.

sanskrit: athāsanāny āviśatāṃ purastād; ubhau virāṭadrupadau narendrau vṛddhaś ca mānyaś ca pṛthivīpatīnāṃ; pitāmaho rāmajanārdanābhyām
english: Then the two foremost lords of men, Virāṭa and Drupada, took their seats in front; and the elder, held in honour among the lords of earth, the Grandsire, took his seat alongside Rāma and Janārdana.

sanskrit: pāñcālarājasya samīpatas tu; śinipravīraḥ saharauhiṇeyaḥ matsyasya rājñas tu susaṃnikṛṣṭau; janārdanaś caiva yudhiṣṭhiraś ca
english: Near the king of the Pāñcālas sat the hero of the Śini clan together with the son of Rohiṇī; and very close to the king of the Matsyas sat Janārdana himself and Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sutāś ca sarve drupadasya rājño; bhīmārjunau mādravatīsutau ca pradyumnasāmbau ca yudhi pravīrau; virāṭaputraś ca sahābhimanyuḥ
english: All the sons of king Drupada, Bhīma and Arjuna, the two sons of Mādravatī, and Pradyumna and Sāmba — both heroes in battle — and the son of Virāṭa together with Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: sarve ca śūrāḥ pitṛbhiḥ samānā; vīryeṇa rūpeṇa balena caiva upāviśan draupadeyāḥ kumārāḥ; suvarṇacitreṣu varāsaneṣu
english: And the young princes, the sons of Draupadī — all heroes equal to their fathers in valour, form, and strength — took their seats upon the excellent seats embellished with gold.

sanskrit: tathopaviṣṭeṣu mahāratheṣu; vibhrājamānāmbarabhūṣaṇeṣu rarāja sā rājavatī samṛddhā; grahair iva dyaur vimalair upetā
english: As those great car-warriors sat there, resplendent in their garments and ornaments, that royal and prosperous hall shone like the sky adorned with bright planets.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathās te samavāyayuktāḥ; kṛtvā vicitrāḥ puruṣapravīrāḥ tasthur muhūrtaṃ paricintayantaḥ; kṛṣṇaṃ nṛpās te samudīkṣamāṇāḥ
english: Then those foremost of men, having engaged in various assembled conversations, stood silent for a moment in thought, those kings gazing upon Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: kathāntam āsādya ca mādhavena; saṃghaṭṭitāḥ pāṇḍavakāryahetoḥ te rājasiṃhāḥ sahitā hy aśṛṇvan; vākyaṃ mahārthaṃ ca mahodayaṃ ca
english: And having reached the end of conversation, stirred together by the Mādhava for the sake of the Pāṇḍava cause, those lion-like kings assembled and heard words of great import and great consequence.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca sarvair bhavadbhir viditaṃ yathāyaṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ saubalenākṣavatyām jito nikṛtyāpahṛtaṃ ca rājyaṃ; punaḥ pravāse samayaḥ kṛtaś ca
english: Kṛṣṇa said: It is known to all of you how Yudhiṣṭhira was defeated at dice by the son of Subala through trickery, and how his kingdom was taken away, and how the compact was made for a further period of exile.

sanskrit: śaktair vijetuṃ tarasā mahīṃ ca; satye sthitais tac caritaṃ yathāvat pāṇḍoḥ sutais tad vratam ugrarūpaṃ; varṣāṇi ṣaṭ sapta ca bhāratāgryaiḥ
english: Though capable of conquering the earth by force, and steadfast in truth, those foremost of the Bhāratas, the sons of Pāṇḍu, fulfilled that severe vow — thirteen years in exile.

sanskrit: trayodaśaś caiva sudustaro 'yam; ajñāyamānair bhavatāṃ samīpe kleśān asahyāṃś ca titikṣamāṇair; yathoṣitaṃ tad viditaṃ ca sarvam
english: And this thirteenth year, most difficult to endure — spent unrecognized in your midst, enduring unbearable hardships — how it was passed is known to all of you.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate dharmasutasya rājño; duryodhanasyāpi ca yad dhitaṃ syāt tac cintayadhvaṃ kurupāṇḍavānāṃ; dharmyaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca yaśaskaraṃ ca
english: Things being so, reflect on what would be beneficial to the son of Dharma as king, and to Duryodhana as well — what is righteous, proper, and honour-winning for the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: adharmayuktaṃ ca na kāmayeta; rājyaṃ surāṇām api dharmarājaḥ dharmārthayuktaṃ ca mahīpatitvaṃ; grāme 'pi kasmiṃś cid ayaṃ bubhūṣet
english: Even the sovereignty of the gods, if tainted by unrighteousness, the king of righteousness would not desire; but lordship over the earth, if coupled with righteousness and right purpose, he would wish to possess even in the smallest village.

sanskrit: pitryaṃ hi rājyaṃ viditaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ; yathāpakṛṣṭaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraputraiḥ mithyopacāreṇa tathāpy anena; kṛcchraṃ mahat prāptam asahyarūpam
english: The ancestral kingdom is known to all kings — how it was wrested away by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra through deceitful means; and yet through all this, great and unbearable hardship has been endured.

sanskrit: na cāpi pārtho vijito raṇe taiḥ; svatejasā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraiḥ tathāpi rājā sahitaḥ suhṛdbhir; abhīpsate 'nāmayam eva teṣām
english: Nor has Pārtha been defeated in battle by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra through their own prowess; and yet the king, together with his friends, wishes for nothing but their well-being.

sanskrit: yat tat svayaṃ pāṇḍusutair vijitya; samāhṛtaṃ bhūmipatīn nipīḍya tat prārthayante puruṣapravīrāḥ; kuntīsutā mādravatīsutau ca
english: What the sons of Pāṇḍu themselves won by conquest, subjugating the lords of the earth and bringing it all together — that is what these foremost of men, the sons of Kuntī and the sons of Mādravatī, now seek.

sanskrit: bālās tv ime tair vividhair upāyaiḥ; saṃprārthitā hantum amitrasāhāḥ rājyaṃ jihīrṣadbhir asadbhir ugraiḥ; sarvaṃ ca tad vo viditaṃ yathāvat
english: But these heroes, though foe-conquering, were set upon by those wicked and violent men using various stratagems, seeking to kill them and seize the kingdom — all of which is fully known to you.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ca lobhaṃ prasamīkṣya vṛddhaṃ; dharmātmatāṃ cāpi yudhiṣṭhirasya saṃbandhitāṃ cāpi samīkṣya teṣāṃ; matiṃ kurudhvaṃ sahitāḥ pṛthak ca
english: Considering the deep greed of those men, and the righteous nature of Yudhiṣṭhira, and also the kinship between them — deliberate, both together and separately, and form your judgment.

sanskrit: ime ca satye 'bhiratā sadaiva; taṃ pārayitvā samayaṃ yathāvat ato 'nyathā tair upacaryamāṇā; hanyuḥ sametān dhṛtarāṣṭraputrān
english: These men, ever devoted to truth, have fulfilled the compact as agreed; yet if treated otherwise by those others, they could destroy the assembled sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tair viprakāraṃ ca niśamya rājñaḥ; suhṛjjanās tān parivārayeyuḥ yuddhena bādheyur imāṃs tathaiva; tair vadhyamānā yudhi tāṃś ca hanyuḥ
english: Hearing of the wrong done by them, the friends of the king would surround them; they would press upon those men with battle; and being attacked by them in war, they would slay them in return.

sanskrit: tathāpi neme 'lpatayā samarthās; teṣāṃ jayāyeti bhaven mataṃ vaḥ sametya sarve sahitāḥ suhṛdbhis; teṣāṃ vināśāya yateyur eva
english: Yet lest the opinion among you be that these men are insufficient for victory over them — let all together, united with their friends, strive for the destruction of those opponents.

sanskrit: duryodhanasyāpi mataṃ yathāvan; na jñāyate kiṃ nu kariṣyatīti ajñāyamāne ca mate parasya; kiṃ syāt samārabhyatamaṃ mataṃ vaḥ
english: The intention of Duryodhana is not truly known — what will he do? And when the intent of the other side is unknown, what course is most to be undertaken in your judgment?

sanskrit: tasmād ito gacchatu dharmaśīlaḥ; śuciḥ kulīnaḥ puruṣo 'pramattaḥ dūtaḥ samarthaḥ praśamāya teṣāṃ; rājyārdhadānāya yudhiṣṭhirasya
english: Therefore let there go from here a man of righteous character, pure, well-born, and vigilant — a capable envoy to seek peace with them and the granting of half the kingdom to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: niśamya vākyaṃ tu janārdanasya; dharmārthayuktaṃ madhuraṃ samaṃ ca samādade vākyam athāgrajo 'sya; saṃpūjya vākyaṃ tad atīva rājan
english: Hearing the words of Janārdana — righteous, purposeful, sweet, and impartial — his elder brother then took up the reply, honouring those words highly, O king.

sanskrit: baladeva uvāca śrutaṃ bhavadbhir gadapūrvajasya; vākyaṃ yathā dharmavad arthavac ca ajātaśatroś ca hitaṃ hitaṃ ca; duryodhanasyāpi tathaiva rājñaḥ
english: Baladeva said: You have heard the words of the elder brother of Gada — how they are righteous and purposeful, and beneficial alike to Ajātaśatru and equally to king Duryodhana.

sanskrit: ardhaṃ hi rājyasya visṛjya vīrāḥ; kuntīsutās tasya kṛte yatante pradāya cārdhaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraputraḥ; sukhī sahāsmābhir atīva modet
english: For the heroes, the sons of Kuntī, strive after giving up half the kingdom on his account; and the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, by granting half, would rejoice greatly in happiness together with us.

sanskrit: labdhvā hi rājyaṃ puruṣapravīrāḥ; samyak pravṛtteṣu pareṣu caiva dhruvaṃ praśāntāḥ sukham āviśeyus; teṣāṃ praśāntiś ca hitaṃ prajānām
english: For having obtained the kingdom, those foremost of men — if the other side conducts themselves rightly — would assuredly find peace and enter into happiness; and their peace is the welfare of the subjects.

sanskrit: duryodhanasyāpi mataṃ ca vettuṃ; vaktuṃ ca vākyāni yudhiṣṭhirasya priyaṃ mama syād yadi tatra kaś cid; vrajec chamārthaṃ kurupāṇḍavānām
english: To learn also the mind of Duryodhana, and to speak the words of Yudhiṣṭhira — it would please me if someone were to go there for the sake of peace between the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sa bhīṣmam āmantrya kurupravīraṃ; vaicitravīryaṃ ca mahānubhāvam droṇaṃ saputraṃ viduraṃ kṛpaṃ ca; gāndhārarājaṃ ca sasūtaputram
english: He should address Bhīṣma, that hero of the Kurus, and the great-souled son of Vichitraveerya, and Droṇa with his son, and Vidura and Kṛpa, and the king of Gāndhāra together with the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: sarve ca ye 'nye dhṛtarāṣṭraputrā; balapradhānā nigamapradhānāḥ sthitāś ca dharmeṣu yathā svakeṣu; lokapravīrāḥ śrutakālavṛddhāḥ
english: And all the other sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra who are foremost in strength and foremost in scriptural learning, who are established in their own respective duties — heroes among men, mature in learning and age.

sanskrit: eteṣu sarveṣu samāgateṣu; paureṣu vṛddheṣu ca saṃgateṣu bravītu vākyaṃ praṇipātayuktaṃ; kuntīsutasyārthakaraṃ yathā syāt
english: When all these are assembled together, and the elders of the city are gathered, let the envoy speak words accompanied with humble salutation, such as would serve the interest of the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: sarvāsv avasthāsu ca te na kauṭyād; grasto hi so 'rtho balam āśritais taiḥ priyābhyupetasya yudhiṣṭhirasya; dyūte pramattasya hṛtaṃ ca rājyam
english: And in all circumstances it was not through deceit on their part but by force that Yudhiṣṭhira's interest was seized — the kingdom was taken by trickery when Yudhiṣṭhira was captivated by the pleasure of the game.

sanskrit: nivāryamāṇaś ca kurupravīraiḥ; sarvaiḥ suhṛdbhir hy ayam apy atajjñaḥ gāndhārarājasya sutaṃ matākṣaṃ; samāhvayed devitum ājamīḍhaḥ
english: Though restrained by all the Kuru heroes and friends, this descendant of Ajamīḍha, being himself ignorant of the game, challenged the skilled dice-player son of the Gāndhāra king to play.

sanskrit: durodarās tatra sahasraśo 'nye; yudhiṣṭhiro yān viṣaheta jetum utsṛjya tān saubalam eva cāyaṃ; samāhvayat tena jito 'kṣavatyām
english: There were thousands of other skilled dice-players whom Yudhiṣṭhira could have endured and beaten; but setting them aside, he challenged Śakuni alone, and by him was defeated at dice.

sanskrit: sa dīvyamānaḥ pratidevanena; akṣeṣu nityaṃ suparāṅmukheṣu saṃrambhamāṇo vijitaḥ prasahya; tatrāparādhaḥ śakuner na kaś cit
english: He played in return, with the dice always turning away from him in ill luck, and being overcome by force in his eagerness — in that matter, no fault belongs to Śakuni.

sanskrit: tasmāt praṇamyaiva vaco bravītu; vaicitravīryaṃ bahusāmayuktam tathā hi śakyo dhṛtarāṣṭraputraḥ; svārthe niyoktuṃ puruṣeṇa tena
english: Therefore let the envoy speak humbly and with much conciliation to the son of Vichitraveerya; for thus is the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra capable of being induced by that man to act in his own proper interest.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bruvaty eva madhupravīre; śinipravīraḥ sahasotpapāta tac cāpi vākyaṃ parinindya tasya; samādade vākyam idaṃ samanyuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as the hero of the Madhu clan spoke thus, the hero of the Śini clan suddenly sprang up, and censuring that speech, took up these words with indignation.

sanskrit: sātyakir uvāca yādṛśaḥ puruṣasyātmā tādṛśaṃ saṃprabhāṣate yathārūpo 'ntarātmā te tathārūpaṃ prabhāṣase
english: Sātyaki said: As a man's inner self is, so he speaks. As your inner self is shaped, so shaped are your words.

sanskrit: santi vai puruṣāḥ śūrāḥ santi kāpuruṣās tathā ubhāv etau dṛḍhau pakṣau dṛśyete puruṣān prati
english: Surely there are brave men and there are cowardly men as well; both these firm tendencies are seen to exist among men.

sanskrit: ekasminn eva jāyete kule klībamahārathau phalāphalavatī śākhe yathaikasmin vanaspatau
english: In one and the same family are born both a eunuch and a great chariot-warrior, just as a tree may have branches bearing fruit and branches without fruit.

sanskrit: nābhyasūyāmi te vākyaṃ bruvato lāṅgaladhvaja ye tu śṛṇvanti te vākyaṃ tān asūyāmi mādhava
english: I do not blame you for speaking such words, O bearer of the plough-banner; but those who listen to your words — them I blame, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi dharmarājasya doṣam alpam api bruvan labhate pariṣanmadhye vyāhartum akutobhayaḥ
english: How can one who speaks even slightly of the faults of the king of righteousness dare to utter such words in the midst of this assembly without fear?

sanskrit: samāhūya mahātmānaṃ jitavanto 'kṣakovidāḥ anakṣajñaṃ yathāśraddhaṃ teṣu dharmajayaḥ kutaḥ
english: Skilled dice-players challenged that great soul, who was not knowledgeable in dice and whose trust was exploited — where is the righteousness in such a victory over him?

sanskrit: yadi kuntīsutaṃ gehe krīḍantaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha abhigamya jayeyus te tat teṣāṃ dharmato bhavet
english: If they had come to the home of the son of Kuntī playing with his brothers and conquered him there — that would have been a victory by dharma for them.

sanskrit: samāhūya tu rājānaṃ kṣatradharmarataṃ sadā nikṛtyā jitavantas te kiṃ nu teṣāṃ paraṃ śubham
english: But having summoned the king who is ever devoted to the Kṣatriya duty and defeated him by trickery — what good fortune can there be for them beyond that?

sanskrit: kathaṃ praṇipatec cāyam iha kṛtvā paṇaṃ param vanavāsād vimuktas tu prāptaḥ paitāmahaṃ padam
english: How should he bow down who, having made the supreme wager, has now been freed from forest exile and has attained the ancestral station?

sanskrit: yady ayaṃ paravittāni kāmayeta yudhiṣṭhiraḥ evam apy ayam atyantaṃ parān nārhati yācitum
english: Even if Yudhiṣṭhira were to covet the wealth of others, even then he would not deserve to beg from his enemies to this extreme degree.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca dharmayuktās te na ca rājyaṃ jihīrṣavaḥ nivṛttavāsān kaunteyān ya āhur viditā iti
english: And how can those who are righteous and not desirous of seizing the kingdom say that the sons of Kuntī, having completed their exile, are recognized and known?

sanskrit: anunītā hi bhīṣmeṇa droṇena ca mahātmanā na vyavasyanti pāṇḍūnāṃ pradātuṃ paitṛkaṃ vasu
english: Though conciliated by Bhīṣma and the great-souled Droṇa, they do not resolve to give the sons of Pāṇḍu their ancestral property.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu tāñ śitair bāṇair anunīya raṇe balāt pādayoḥ pātayiṣyāmi kaunteyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: But I, conciliating them with sharp arrows, shall by force in battle make them fall at the feet of that great-souled son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: atha te na vyavasyanti praṇipātāya dhīmataḥ gamiṣyanti sahāmātyā yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: If they do not resolve to bow down before the wise one, they shall go along with their ministers to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: na hi te yuyudhānasya saṃrabdhasya yuyutsataḥ vegaṃ samarthāḥ saṃsoḍhuṃ vajrasyeva mahīdharāḥ
english: For they are not capable of withstanding the fury of the wrathful and battle-eager Yuyudhāna, just as mountains cannot withstand the velocity of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: ko hi gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ kaś ca cakrāyudhaṃ yudhi māṃ cāpi viṣahet ko nu kaś ca bhīmaṃ durāsadam
english: Who indeed can endure in battle the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow, or the wielder of the discus weapon? And who can endure me, and who can endure Bhīma, who is difficult to approach?

sanskrit: yamau ca dṛḍhadhanvānau yamakalpau mahādyutī ko jijīviṣur āsīded dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam
english: And the twin brothers, wielders of firm bows, of great splendour, comparable to the god of death — what man wishing to live would approach them, or Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the son of Pṛṣata?

sanskrit: pañcemān pāṇḍaveyāṃś ca draupadyāḥ kīrtivardhanān samapramāṇān pāṇḍūnāṃ samavīryān madotkaṭān
english: These five Pāṇḍavas, and the five sons of Draupadī who enhance her glory, equal in measure to the sons of Pāṇḍu, equal in valour, drunk with battle-ardour —

sanskrit: saubhadraṃ ca maheṣvāsam amarair api duḥsaham gadapradyumnasāmbāṃś ca kālavajrānalopamān
english: — and the great archer Saubhadra, difficult to bear even for the immortals, and Gada, Pradyumna, and Sāmba, comparable to the thunderbolt of Death, unassailable —

sanskrit: te vayaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraṃ śakuninā saha karṇena ca nihatyājāv abhiṣekṣyāma pāṇḍavam
english: — we, having slain in battle the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with Śakuni and Karṇa, shall consecrate the Pāṇḍava king.

sanskrit: nādharmo vidyate kaś cic chatrūn hatvātatāyinaḥ adharmyam ayaśasyaṃ ca śātravāṇāṃ prayācanam
english: There is no unrighteousness whatsoever in slaying enemies who are aggressors; it is unrighteous and dishonourable to beg from enemies.

sanskrit: hṛdgatas tasya yaḥ kāmas taṃ kurudhvam atandritāḥ nisṛṣṭaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājyaṃ prāpnotu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Fulfil diligently whatever desire lies in his heart; let the Pāṇḍava obtain the kingdom that was surrendered by Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: adya pāṇḍusuto rājyaṃ labhatāṃ vā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nihatā vā raṇe sarve svapsyanti vasudhātale
english: Today let Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Pāṇḍu obtain the kingdom, or let all of them be slain in battle and sleep upon the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca evam etan mahābāho bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ na hi duryodhano rājyaṃ madhureṇa pradāsyati
english: Drupada said: So it shall be, O mighty-armed one — there is no doubt. For Duryodhana will not give up the kingdom through gentle persuasion.

sanskrit: anuvartsyati taṃ cāpi dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ sutapriyaḥ bhīṣmadroṇau ca kārpaṇyān maurkhyād rādheyasaubalau
english: And Dhṛtarāṣṭra, fond of his son, will follow him; and Bhīṣma and Droṇa out of weakness; and the son of Rādhā and the son of Subala out of folly.

sanskrit: baladevasya vākyaṃ tu mama jñāne na yujyate etad dhi puruṣeṇāgre kāryaṃ sunayam icchatā
english: Baladeva's speech, in my judgment, is not appropriate; for this is indeed what should be done first by a man who desires sound policy.

sanskrit: na tu vācyo mṛdu vaco dhārtarāṣṭraḥ kathaṃ cana na hi mārdavasādhyo 'sau pāpabuddhir mato mama
english: Gentle words, however, should by no means be spoken to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; for in my view that evil-minded one is not to be won over by mildness.

sanskrit: gardabhe mārdavaṃ kuryād goṣu tīkṣṇaṃ samācaret mṛdu duryodhane vākyaṃ yo brūyāt pāpacetasi
english: One might show gentleness to a donkey and employ sharpness toward cattle; but whoever would speak mild words to Duryodhana of wicked mind —

sanskrit: mṛdu vai manyate pāpo bhāṣyamāṇam aśaktijam jitam arthaṃ vijānīyād abudho mārdave sati
english: — the wicked man would think the gentle speech springs from weakness; the fool would consider the matter won when met with mildness.

sanskrit: etac caiva kariṣyāmo yatnaś ca kriyatām iha prasthāpayāma mitrebhyo balāny udyojayantu naḥ
english: This therefore we shall do, and let effort be made here: let us send word to our allies and let them mobilise forces for us.

sanskrit: śalyasya dhṛṣṭaketoś ca jayatsenasya cābhibhoḥ kekayānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ dūtā gacchantu śīghragāḥ
english: To Śalya, and to Dhṛṣṭaketu, and to Jayatsena, and to all the Kekayas — let swift messengers go.

sanskrit: sa tu duryodhano nūnaṃ preṣayiṣyati sarvaśaḥ pūrvābhipannāḥ santaś ca bhajante pūrvacodakam
english: For Duryodhana will surely send word everywhere; and those who have been previously approached tend to side with the one who solicited them first.

sanskrit: tat tvaradhvaṃ narendrāṇāṃ pūrvam eva pracodane mahad dhi kāryaṃ voḍhavyam iti me vartate matiḥ
english: Therefore make haste to solicit the lords of men before he does; it is my firm conviction that a great task is to be accomplished.

sanskrit: śalyasya preṣyatāṃ śīghraṃ ye ca tasyānugā nṛpāḥ bhagadattāya rājñe ca pūrvasāgaravāsine
english: Let word be sent swiftly to Śalya and the kings who follow him, and to king Bhagadatta who dwells by the eastern sea.

sanskrit: amitaujase tathogrāya hārdikyāyāhukāya ca dīrghaprajñāya mallāya rocamānāya cābhibho
english: To Amitojas and to the fierce Ugra, and to Hārdikya and Āhuka, and to the far-sighted Malla and to Rocamāna, O lord.

sanskrit: ānīyatāṃ bṛhantaś ca senābinduś ca pārthivaḥ pāpajit prativindhyaś ca citravarmā suvāstukaḥ
english: Let Bṛhanta and king Senābindu be brought, and Papajit and Prativindhya, and Chitravarma and Suvastuka.

sanskrit: bāhlīko muñjakeśaś ca caidyādhipatir eva ca supārśvaś ca subāhuś ca pauravaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Bāhlika and Munjakesa, and the lord of the Cedis, and Suparshva and Subāhu, and Pourava the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: śakānāṃ pahlavānāṃ ca daradānāṃ ca ye nṛpāḥ kāmbojā ṛṣikā ye ca paścimānūpakāś ca ye
english: The kings of the Śakas, the Pahlavas, and the Daradas; the Kāmbojas, the Rishikas, and those of the western riverine regions.

sanskrit: jayatsenaś ca kāśyaś ca tathā pañcanadā nṛpāḥ krāthaputraś ca durdharṣaḥ pārvatīyāś ca ye nṛpāḥ
english: And Jayatsena and the king of Kāśi, and likewise the kings of the five rivers, and the irresistible son of Krātha, and the mountain kings.

sanskrit: jānakiś ca suśarmā ca maṇimān pautimatsyakaḥ pāṃsurāṣṭrādhipaś caiva dhṛṣṭaketuś ca vīryavān
english: And Jānakī and Suśarmā and Maṇimān and Pautimatsyaka, and the lord of the Pamsurashra, and the valiant Dhṛṣṭaketu.

sanskrit: auḍraś ca daṇḍadhāraś ca bṛhatsenaś ca vīryavān aparājito niṣādaś ca śreṇimān vasumān api
english: And Audra and Daṇḍadhāra, and the valiant Brhatsena, and Aparajita and the Niṣāda king, and Śreṇimān and Vasuman.

sanskrit: bṛhadbalo mahaujāś ca bāhuḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ samudraseno rājā ca saha putreṇa vīryavān
english: And Bṛhadbala and Mahaujas, and Bahu and Parapuramjaya, and king Samudrasena together with his valiant son.
